body.statement:
For an admissible fixed choice of class constants with \(H=0\), \(p=S=d=1\), \(\lambda=\kappa=1\), and the uniform order-zero kernel \(K\), there is a triangular array of laws in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)\), with \(n_1=N=T^2\), for which
\[
R_\star=T^{-2},\qquad
\lim_{T\to\infty}\mathbb E\!\left[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0\right]=\frac{3}{16}.
\]
In the same array, the event multiplier radius satisfies \(r_{\mathrm{tr}}=0\) almost surely even though the conditional variance of the centered event contribution is \(3/16\).
Moreover, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\),
\[
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
body.proof_tex:
It is enough to exhibit one legal choice of the fixed constants, because the asserted frontier is stated for every law in the displayed class.  Take \(B=16\), \(c_X=C_X=1\), \(c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\), \(\delta_0=1/4\), \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}=C_{\mathrm{mod}}=1\), and \(L\ge1\).  Let \(E_0\) be constant, put \(z_0=1/2\), and take \(\mathcal Z_+=\{1/2\}\).  Let \((X_t)_{t=1}^{T}\) be independent uniform random variables on \([0,1]\).  Set
\[
m(x)=8+x-\frac12,
\qquad
Q_{ti}=m(X_t)+\frac12 U_{ti},
\]
where the \(U_{ti}\) are independent Rademacher variables, independent of the design.  Finally, let the donors be
\[
Z_j=\frac12+V_j,
\]
where the \(V_j\) are independent Rademacher variables independent of all historical variables.

These choices give \(0\le Q_{ti}\le16\),
\(\mathbb E[Q_{ti}\mid X_t,E_0]=m(X_t)\), and
\(\operatorname{Var}(Q_{ti}-m(X_t)\mid X_t,E_0)=1/4\ge B^{-1}\).  The design density is one, and the calendar process is independent over \(t\), hence its conditional beta-mixing coefficients vanish.  Also
\[
\mathbb E[Z_j\mid E_0]=z_0,qquad
\Sigma=1,qquad
\mathbb E[|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)|^4\mid E_0]=1\le B.
\]
Exact training coordinates are obtained by setting \(X_t^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_t\).

For \(0<\delta\le1/4\), the constraint in \texttt{def:local-modulus} is \(|u|\le\delta\), and both \(z_0+u\) and \(z_0-u\) remain in \([0,1]\).  Since \(m(z_0+u)-m(z_0)=u\),
\[
\omega_P(\delta;z_0)=\sup_{|u|\le\delta}|u|=\delta.
\]
Thus both sides of \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus} hold with \(\kappa=1\); the Holder, interior, ellipticity, fourth-moment, and positive-query requirements also hold.

Define \(G=\mathbf 1\{X_1\le1/4\}\) and, for every event unit \(i\), set
\[
B_i(0)=8,qquad B_i(1)=8+G,qquad B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_i(1).
\]
These wealth levels lie in \([0,16]\).  They can be represented by \texttt{def:buyhold-level} by taking \(W_{i,-1}=1\) and \(R_{i0}(a)=B_i(a)-1>-1\).  Set every historical potential outcome equal to the displayed untreated \(Q_{ti}\), independently of its path-status label.  Consistency, historical consistency, limited anticipation, and no spillovers then hold.  Event transport holds because
\[
n_1^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}\mathbb E[B_i(0)\mid z_0,E_0]=8=m(z_0).
\]
Conditional on the complete design path, the event outcomes are constants and the historical error paths are independent across \(i\).  Hence the unit vectors consisting of a historical path and its event outcome are conditionally independent, exactly as required by \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}; within-site replication is immediate.  Donor independence also holds.  This verifies membership in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(1)\).

Because \(G\) is Bernoulli with success probability \(1/4\), \texttt{def:target} gives
\[
\tau_n(z_0)=\mathbb E[B_i(1)-B_i(0)\mid z_0,E_0]=\frac14,
\qquad
\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}=8+G.
\]
We next verify the only estimator fact needed for the counterexample.  For \(n_1=N=T^2\), the initial bandwidth is
\[
h_1=(T^3)^{-1/3}\vee T^{-1}\vee(T^2)^{-1/2}=T^{-1}.
\]
Projection is nonexpansive, so every complementary-fold center is \(1/2+O_{L^2}(T^{-1})\).  Conditional on such a center, the nearest-neighbor distance among \(T\) independent uniform design points is \(O_{L^2}(T^{-1})\).  With \(K(u)=\mathbf 1\{|u|\le1\}\) and \(r=0\), the dyadic selection rule therefore chooses \(h_{1k}=O_{L^2}(T^{-1})\); once one design point enters the window, its \(n_1=T^2\) replicated rows make the scalar Gram matrix exceed the fixed success threshold.  Conditional on the selected design points, the fitted intercept is a convex combination of their within-site averages.  Its squared bias relative to \(m(1/2)\) is \(O(T^{-2})\), while independence of the \(U_{ti}\) gives conditional variance at most \(1/(4n_1)=O(T^{-2})\).  Averaging a fixed number of donor folds preserves this order.  Hence
\[
\widehat m_1-m(1/2)=O_{L^2}(T^{-1}).
\]
The raw estimator consequently satisfies
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
=G-\frac14-\{\widehat m_1-m(1/2)\},
\]
and Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
\lim_{T\to\infty}\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
=\mathbb E[(G-1/4)^2]=\frac{3}{16}.
\]
On the other hand, with \(\pi_1=1\), \(n_1=N=T^2\), and \(\lambda=d=\kappa=1\),
\[
R_{\mathrm{tr}}=T^{-2},\quad
R_{\mathrm{sm}}=(T^3)^{-2/3}=T^{-2},\quad
R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2},\quad
R_{\mathrm{don}}=T^{-2},
\]
so \(R_\star=T^{-2}\).  Finally all event observations equal \(8+G\), whence
\[
E_{1i}=n_1^{-1}(B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}})=0
\]
for every \(i\).  Therefore \(G_{\mathrm{tr}}^{\#}=0\) and \(r_{\mathrm{tr}}=0\), although \(\operatorname{Var}(G-1/4\mid E_0)=3/16\).  The witness isolates the missing conditional-mean stability: conditioning on the full design makes the units independent but does not make their event means stable after the design is integrated out.

It remains to verify the asserted failure of the reported interval.  The retained set has cardinality of order \(T\).  Uniformly over the full fit and the \(M=O(T^{2/3})\) delete-one-block fits, a union bound for uniform nearest-neighbor spacings gives selected bandwidth
\[
O_P\!\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right).
\]
For any selected local-constant fit, conditional on its design and donor center, its noise is a convex combination of within-site averages of \(n_1=T^2\) independent Rademacher variables scaled by \(1/2\).  The elementary inequality \(\cosh(x)\le e^{x^2/2}\), applied to the conditional moment-generating function, makes this noise sub-Gaussian with variance proxy at most \(1/(4n_1)\).  A union bound over the \(M+1\) fits therefore shows that the maximum fitted-noise magnitude is
\[
O_P\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{n_1}}\right)
=O_P\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{\log(T\vee2)}}{T}\right).
\]
Thus the maximum difference between the full retained fit and any delete-block fit is \(O_P(\log(T\vee2)/T)\).  Since \(M=O(T^{2/3})\), the definitions of \(J_b\) and \(C_b\) imply
\[
\max_{b\le M}|C_b|=O_P\!\left(\frac{M\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right)=o_P(1).
\]
For every multiplier realization,
\[
|G_{\mathrm{cal}}^{\#}|
\le\{M(M-1)\}^{-1/2}\sum_{b=1}^{M}|C_b|
\le\sqrt{\frac{M}{M-1}}\max_{b\le M}|C_b|,
\]
so \(r_{\mathrm{cal}}=o_P(1)\).  For the order-zero fit, successful local-constant weights are nonnegative and sum to one.  Consequently the deterministic Taylor allowance satisfies
\[
A_L=O_P\!\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right),
\]
and the donor formula with \(m_k\asymp N=T^2\) gives \(A_{\mathrm{don}}=O(T^{-1})\).  All declared bad-sample conditions are absent with probability tending to one: \(M\ge3\) and \(m_k\ge1\) eventually, the scalar Gram search succeeds by bandwidth one for every full and delete-block fit, every constructed quantity is finite, spectral clipping is defined, and \(\max_k\delta_k\le\delta_0\) eventually.  Hence
\[
H_\alpha=o_P(1),qquad \widehat\tau_R\longrightarrow G
\quad\text{in probability}.
\]
Because \(|G-1/4|\ge1/4\) almost surely, the interval coverage tends to zero.  This proves that the frozen honest-interval claim, not merely its proposed proof route, fails on the declared class.
